rules.semantic_labels: Normalize only decorative edge whitespace; match the complete semantic title. Treat adjacent parameter titles and value-only buttons as separate elements unless the observed hierarchy combines them.
rules.foreground_scope: Resolve the current foreground container and element type before reading or acting. Do not infer an accessibility type from visible text; OS choices may be Buttons inside a CollectionView rather than StaticText. Review every remaining interaction, not just the failing line. Multi-selection may use Table Cells containing entity StaticText even when single-selection uses CollectionView Buttons; inspect the actual presenter. Native submenu leaf buttons can omit source IDs even when the parent menu exports its ID. When terminal hierarchy proves this, use the complete observed semantic title in the menu CollectionView/Cell/Button structure via menuActions/tapTestMenuAction; do not retry an absent ID or pick the first match. In-flight sync status can appear both in the deck-list footer and the bottom busy bar. Match the observed collection-scoped status, retaining uniqueness; never use a global first match to bypass these repeated labels.
rules.unique_reads_and_actions: Both passive reads and actions use one foreground-scoped match. Observations need a visible frame; actions additionally require enabled/hittable. Never pick the first duplicate. Source IDs may not be exported by native alert fields. For observed nested action wrappers, select direct children of the action container; containing a same-ID element is not proof of uniqueness. Keep hit testing in object readiness, not a literal query predicate. Run check-ui-query-predicates.py before CI. Native SwiftUI Switch rows can wrap a separate direct Switch child without an ID. Use setTestSwitch to act on the unique child and verify its value; a hittable labelled row does not establish the actual switch hit point. Confirmation popovers can export a Sheet containing the same nested same-ID Button wrappers as native alerts. Scope to the observed Popover/Sheet and use the shared direct-Other/child-Button action resolver, rather than a global ID or arbitrary first wrapper. WebKit can expose several nested WebView wrappers with identical frames for one review card. Resolve the native Other host’s direct WebView through waitForTestCardWebView, then retain unique/actionable checks and app-anchored screen coordinates. Do not use all WebView descendants or an arbitrary first wrapper. A query waiter timing out does not prove a terminal duplicate or missing target. Re-evaluate the same unique predicate and actual enabled/hittable or visible-frame predicate before failing; terminal AX can show one valid target after the last waiter observation. Preserve zero/duplicate/disabled/offscreen failures and evidence; do not extend timeouts or select a first match.
rules.live_state: Require the expected live data or completed transition. Placeholder, redaction, and element existence alone do not establish readiness. Native empty TextField.value may equal placeholderValue: prove empty input with the shared insertion/full-result helper, not a placeholder-only equality. Use requireTestCondition for new semantic transition waits: recheck the same current postcondition after a deadline and retain terminal hierarchy/screenshot on failure, as with control lookups. A timeout assertion containing only debugDescription can omit a failure screenshot. Model flags alone do not prove the native consumer received the same environment: compare List selection state and EditButton appearance with actual binding callbacks; supply one owned edit-mode binding at the consumers rather than ignoring legitimate deselection events. DOM focus and AX Focused do not alone prove native keyboard routing: retain actual full input and rendered-answer checks; do not add a tap or inject an answer to conceal a broken automatic-focus path.
rules.keyboard_and_scroll: Use shared keyboard and reveal handling; retain explicit postconditions for optional transient UI. Keyboard query count/exists alone is not visibility: the OS can retain a zero-height offscreen node. Use object isHittable (false when missing/offscreen) without a separate exists-to-frame dereference. Do not put hittable in matching predicates. A waiter observation timeout is not a current-state verdict: before failing, recheck the same keyboard-closed or unique-actionable dismissal postcondition; never bypass uniqueness or actual keyboard closure. A hidden software Keyboard does not prove that the native text responder or input-assistant/password bar is inactive. If an exact native control tap lands inside its visible frame without a state change, retain responder/accessory state and binding callbacks; do not substitute another tap or assume the first tap activated the control. Input helpers preserve the keyboard while editing a foreground native alert; ordinary forms retain their reveal/dismiss handling. Never try to hide it through a control outside an intended foreground native alert: XCTest may classify that alert as an interruption and cancel unsaved input. Alert actions retain keyboard policy keep, and generic dismissal must fail with evidence rather than triggering that cancellation. A lazy native form may omit rows above the viewport entirely. When revisiting a known earlier setting after reading the bottom status, pass the earlier-row search direction to the shared reveal helper; a missing AX node does not justify repeatedly scrolling toward the same bottom boundary. Preserve reveal bounds and native switch/value checks. Form-reveal failure must retain its target query, direction, terminal hierarchy and screen.
rules.environment: Check actual fixtures, services, onboarding and dependencies, including simulator team/App ID/bundle consistency and the remote consumer’s shared-data context, before long UI work. After the final common-helper or case edit, rerun syntax, complete UI case-manifest/selection validation, query lint and workflow dispatch-choice coverage before dispatch. Helpers must not start with the XCTest test prefix; a previous pre-edit check is not evidence for changed source. When adding/changing AppText.localized labels, including DEBUG diagnostics, run localization_resources_smoke.py on final source before dispatch. Match existing interpolation types/keys; Swift parse/catalog checks do not verify resource coverage. A verified compiled widget must include its exported native AppIntents configuration metadata before long UI. When a native capability passes in focused project execution but fails in relocated consumers, compare the actual launch entrypoint using the same producer products and project; do not equate an authorized status with accepted OS registration.
rules.first_failure_evidence: Compare hierarchy, recording and coordinates before changing an interaction; capture remote-process logs during the test because runner cleanup can stop its simulator; retain bounded persistent probes and repair missing diagnostics before another attempt. Compare the terminal failure capture as well as the immediate transition capture; a transient spinner does not prove persistent loading. If synthesized pointer coordinates already hit the actual unique control, do not try another tap variant: classify the remaining cause as undetermined and observe binding setters/state/lifecycle and numeric input events before changing behavior. Failure screenshots use the screen capture when the application may have exited; do not replace the original app-crash failure with an error requesting a screenshot from a non-running app. Preserve first assertion/uncaught-exception events in a separate bounded critical log before later cases can displace them from the rolling live log; inspect truncation flags and actual crash attachments rather than inferring missing exception text. Preserve the first native notification authorization failure in the bounded critical capture as well; current authorizationStatus alone does not prove the OS accepted request registration. Read native responder/binding diagnostic values directly, since debugDescription may truncate AX values. Synthetic diagnostics must not drive periodic SwiftUI updates during an interaction: expose an on-demand accessibility value instead, keep fields non-sensitive and preserve real input/OS assertions. Include app-main-bundle/SpringBoard source-registration logs when notification permission succeeds but OS request storage fails.
rules.failure_classification: Separate app defects, harness defects, environment failures and inspection failures; count repeat attempts. Read actual crash process identity and stack: app UIKit abort and XCTest runner crash-log tracking failure are different; a missing control after app termination is not evidence for a selector repair. Order completed validation attempts by actual executed step start records, not mutable run-level updated_at or inconsistent run/job metadata clocks. Include earlier rerun attempts even when their run ID predates newer runs, preserve intervening UI success resets, and exclude gate-only rejections. Missing chronology evidence must fail closed.
rules.runtime_warnings: A passed assertion does not dispose of application runtime warnings.
rules.device_evidence: Simulator checks do not prove actual audio, notification delivery, re-signing or device permissions.
